title: At the Pottery Bench
description: Explore familiar pottery words for clay, vessels, shaping forms, and their parts.
cardDescription: Explore familiar pottery words for clay, vessels, shaping forms, and their parts.
focus: The clues name materials and objects rather than a making procedure. The shape or location of a part identifies it.
solvingTip: Look for a material, a vessel, or one part of a container.
words: Earth material shaped and fired to make pottery
Rounded vessel made from a material such as clay
Pottery container often used to display flowers
Rotating support used in some pottery making
High-temperature oven used to fire pottery
Coating fired onto pottery to change its surface
Part of a clay mug used for holding it
Upper edge of a pottery vessel
Bottom supporting part of a pot
To heat pottery in a kiln
To lose moisture before or during part of a making process

answerNotes.KILN: A kiln is an oven designed for processes such as firing pottery. It is not the rotating pottery wheel.
answerNotes.COIL: Coil names a long rolled clay form. It differs from a flat slab.
answerNotes.GLAZE: Pottery glaze is a fired surface coating. The clue uses a craft material rather than a food topping.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim is the upper edge. The base is the bottom support, so location distinguishes them.

title: Paper on the Craft Table
description: Explore familiar paper tools, simple shapes, and the names of folding and pasted-picture crafts.
cardDescription: Explore familiar paper tools, simple shapes, and the names of folding and pasted-picture crafts.
focus: The clues distinguish materials from actions and finished forms. Direct definitions introduce the two named paper arts.
solvingTip: Look for an object, an edge, a folding mark, or a whole craft form.
words: Thin sheet material used for folding and pasting
To bend a sheet back over itself
Line made by sharply folding paper
To divide paper with a blade or scissors
Hand tool with paired blades for cutting a sheet
Adhesive used to join paper pieces
Stiffer paper used for a greeting or craft support
Outer boundary of a paper sheet
Place where two paper edges meet
Long narrow piece cut from paper
One complete flat piece of paper
Guide showing a craft design or shape
Picture made by arranging and attaching separate materials
Art of forming shapes by folding paper

answerNotes.ORIGAMI: Origami is paper folding. Its name identifies an art form rather than one particular folded object.
answerNotes.COLLAGE: Collage combines attached pieces into a picture. It differs from drawing every element directly on the surface.
answerNotes.CREASE: A crease is the mark made by a fold. The clue asks for the resulting line.
answerNotes.SHEET: A sheet is one flat piece of material. It differs from a narrow strip cut from that piece.

title: Pieces in a Mosaic
description: Build a vocabulary picture through familiar mosaic pieces, surfaces, and joining materials.
cardDescription: Build a vocabulary picture through familiar mosaic pieces, surfaces, and joining materials.
focus: The clues identify objects by how they relate to a larger design. Some answers name a whole work; others name a small part.
solvingTip: Look for a design, one piece, or a material occupying the spaces between pieces.
words: Design assembled from many small separate pieces
Small flat unit used in many mosaics
Material used for bright or translucent mosaic pieces
Natural hard material cut into mosaic units
Material filling spaces between set tiles
Arrangement repeated or planned across a design
One separate unit in a mosaic
Visible hue used to organize a design
Outer area on which mosaic pieces are placed
Decorative band around a mosaic’s outside
Outer limit of a tile or finished design
Substance bonding a tile to its support

answerNotes.GROUT: Grout fills the spaces between tiles. Adhesive attaches the tiles to their support instead.
answerNotes.MOSAIC: A mosaic is the assembled design. It can use materials such as stone, glass, or ceramic.
answerNotes.TILE: A tile is one flat unit here. The clue does not name the entire finished mosaic.
answerNotes.ADHESIVE: Adhesive is a general word for a bonding substance. It is distinct from the support beneath the design.

title: Pressed Flowers in a Frame
description: Explore a pressed-flower keepsake through plant parts, paper, supports, and arranging words.
cardDescription: Explore a pressed-flower keepsake through plant parts, paper, supports, and arranging words.
focus: The clues describe objects used around a familiar craft. A plant part and the object displaying it have separate names.
solvingTip: Look for a plant feature, a support, or an action used to arrange a display.
words: Device applying steady pressure to flatten material
Plant bloom preserved in a decorative keepsake
One often colorful part of a flower
Flat plant part placed beside a pressed bloom
Plant support attached beneath a flower
Thin material placed around flowers in a press
Bound pages sometimes used as a flat weight
Heavy object applying pressure from above
To lose moisture from plant material
Border holding a finished pressed-flower display
Stiff paper support for a small arrangement
To place separate items into a planned design
Planned visual arrangement of a craft
Object preserved as a reminder of a person or event

answerNotes.PRESS: Press is a pressure-applying device here. It is a noun rather than the action of pushing a button.
answerNotes.KEEPSAKE: A keepsake is retained for its personal association. Its meaning is not limited to one material or craft.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaf names a plant part in this clue. It does not mean one sheet of a book.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame supports the finished display. It is separate from the plant material arranged inside.

title: A Miniature Village
description: Explore a small model scene through familiar building parts, materials, and size words.
cardDescription: Explore a small model scene through familiar building parts, materials, and size words.
focus: The clues name objects in a miniature setting. The model represents a larger object rather than being used as the full-size building.
solvingTip: Look for a whole model, a building feature, a support, or a making material.
words: Small representation of a larger object or scene
Ratio between a model’s dimensions and the represented object
Small building represented in a village scene
Upper covering of a model building
Upright side of a miniature building
Entrance represented on a model house
Glazed-opening shape shown in a tiny building
Model structure carrying a route across a gap
Plant form added to a small landscape scene
Colored coating applied to a miniature object
Supporting platform beneath a model scene
Small feature added to make a model more specific

answerNotes.SCALE: Scale is the size ratio in this clue. It is not a weighing instrument.
answerNotes.MODEL: A model represents something else. The word names the small representation rather than the full-size object.
answerNotes.BASE: The base supports the scene. It differs from one building or road placed on it.
answerNotes.DETAIL: A detail is a smaller feature within the whole. The clue asks for the general word rather than a particular tiny object.
